answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a paid registration bond rather than identity checks. Each new agent identity must lock a meaningful stake for a long epoch, so spinning up thousands of puppets means capital sitting idle in every one of them. The cost scales linearly while the expected reward per identity does not, and any proven duplicate or colluding cluster gets its bond slashed and burned. The dune of cheap throwaway accounts therefore collapses, and an attacker must front real funds across a long thread of epochs to hold the sable of reputation, making farms unprofitable.
